compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: RTX5090 (Blackwell): high BW HBM/GDDR7, large L2, fp16 tensor cores, lots of SMs. Output spatial 360x640=230400 per channel, 32 out ch, batch=1.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Conv3x3 with Cin=16, Cout=32, K=3 -> 16*3*3=144 MACs per output pixel. Weights total = 32*16*9 = 4608 fp16 = 9KB, easily fits in shared/constant memory.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Low arithmetic intensity, mostly memory-bound; ReLU+AvgPool fuse trivially.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Input 1*16*720*1280*2B = ~29MB; output after pool 1*32*360*640*2B = ~14.7MB. Conv intermediate (before pool) would be 1*32*720*1280*2B = ~59MB if materialized.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Materializing intermediates kills BW; must fuse Conv+ReLU+AvgPool into one kernel.

register_pressure.notes: Weights small (9KB) fit in shared. Per-thread accumulators for 2x2 pool block * Cout tile manageable.
register_pressure.risk: If tiling Cout fully per thread, regs may spill; tile Cout in chunks.

nodes.notes: 1) Classification: fused stencil (3x3 conv) + elementwise (ReLU) + reduction (2x2 avg pool). Dense, contiguous NCHW fp16. 2) Math: out[n,co,oh,ow] = avg_{2x2}( relu( sum_{ci,kh,kw} in[n,ci,2oh+kh-?,2ow+kw-?] * W[co,ci,kh,kw] + b[co] ) ). Conv stride1 pad1 then 2x2 avgpool stride2 => each output pixel needs a 4x4 input neighborhood per Cin channel (2x2 conv windows that share rows/cols). 3) Layout: NCHW fp16 contiguous. Input [1,16,720,1280]; weights [32,16,3,3] tiny -> shared/constant; output [1,32,360,640]. Heavy reuse across 2x2 pool window and across Cout. 4) Regimes: (a) memory-bound full image (current) — BW limited, fusion critical; (b) weight-reuse limited if Cout tile small — recompute conv 4x; (c) register-spill regime if tile too large. 5) Knobs: output tile (OHxOW per block), Cout tile per thread/block, shared-mem caching of input halo, vectorized fp16x2 loads, tensor-core MMA for 16->32 reduction, async copies. 6) Skeleton: one kernel; each block computes a tile of pooled outputs for a Cout-tile; loads input halo (tile*2+2 in each dim) into shared once across all Cout; loops Cin inside, accumulates conv into per-thread 2x2 buffer, ReLU then averages, writes pooled output. 7) Families: (A) Fully-fused shared-memory conv+pool with Cin-loop in registers (TOP — full working set fits: weights 9KB + halo tile ~few KB); (B) Tensor-core MMA fused (im2col-on-the-fly within shared); (C) Two-pass (conv->relu fused, then pool) — rejected as wastes BW.

action.description: Single fused CUDA kernel: each block produces a tile of pooled outputs (e.g., 16x32 pooled pixels = 32x64 conv pixels) for ALL 32 output channels. Load input halo (34x66 per Cin) into shared memory, iterate Cin=16, compute 2x2 conv outputs per thread, apply ReLU, average into 1 pooled output. Weights in constant or shared memory. Use fp16 arithmetic with fp32 accumulators.
action.rationale: Eliminates intermediate writes; weights are tiny so full Cout fusion is trivial; halo reuse across 2x2 pool reduces redundant input reads by ~4x vs naive.
action.title: Fully-fused Conv+ReLU+AvgPool single kernel with shared-mem halo

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: RTX5090 abundant SMs; 230400 pooled pixels / tile_size blocks. Cout=32 maps to warp-friendly sizes.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Good occupancy; can use FMA on fp16x2.

memory_bandwidth.risk: Halo overlap between blocks adds ~10-20% extra reads.

action.description: Variant of full fusion using __half2 vectorized loads/stores and HFMA2 for the Cin reduction. Pair Cin channels two-at-a-time; load input as half2 along channel dim (after a small layout shuffle or via two pointers). Weights packed as half2 per (ci,ci+1) pair. Accumulate in float for stability.
action.rationale: Doubles effective compute throughput on fp16 ALU path; halves shared-memory bank pressure for weights.
action.title: Vectorized half2 fused kernel

action.description: Use tensor-core WMMA/MMA to perform the Cin reduction. Treat each output spatial tile as M dim, Cout=32 as N, Cin*Kh*Kw=144 as K. Build an implicit-GEMM where shared-memory holds an im2col-ish patch tile (computed on the fly from halo) and weights tile; fuse ReLU+AvgPool in epilogue.
action.rationale: Tensor cores provide highest fp16 throughput; Cout=32 fits one warp's MMA-N dimension nicely. Epilogue fusion preserves BW savings.
action.title: WMMA implicit-GEMM fused conv+relu+pool

kernel_summary: Fused Conv2d(3x3, pad=1) -> ReLU -> AvgPool2d(2x2) on fp16 NCHW input [1,16,720,1280] producing [1,32,360,640]. Weights are tiny (32x16x3x3 = 9KB) so they fully fit in shared/constant memory. The kernel is dominated by global memory bandwidth for the input (~29MB) and pooled output (~14.7MB); the conv intermediate (~59MB) must NOT be materialized. Full fusion is mandatory and feasible: each thread block computes a tile of pooled outputs for all 32 output channels, loads an input halo into shared memory once, iterates over Cin=16, applies ReLU, and writes the 2x2-averaged result. Key constraints: fp16 precision (tol 0.01), NCHW contiguous, batch=1, kernel must match reference outputs.
open_questions: Optimal output-tile size (pooled pixels per block) balancing shared-memory halo size, occupancy, and reuse?
Should weights live in __constant__ memory (9KB fits) or shared memory loaded once per block?
Is fp32 accumulation required to stay within rtol/atol=0.01, or does fp16 accumulation suffice given small Cin=16?
Best Cout sub-tiling (8 vs 16 vs 32 per thread) to avoid register spill while maximizing weight reuse?
Can WMMA tensor cores beat CUDA-core HFMA2 given this is likely memory-bound, or is the setup cost prohibitive?
Are async copies (cp.async) on Blackwell worth using to overlap halo loads with compute for this small kernel?
Does the input need any layout transform (e.g., channels-last or half2-packed along C) to maximize coalesced loads?
How much does halo overlap between adjacent blocks inflate total input reads, and can we mitigate via larger tiles?
